clue.text: Punitive action to restrict duke is what egalitarians want

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the punishment word closes around the other pieces

parts.note: retribution is punishment dealt out in return
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone argues that egalitarians really want punishment that curbs the power of a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to restrict' has the punishment word closing round 'duke is'; 'Punitive action' looks like the definition, but the definition is the egalitarians' aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Egalitarians seek a sharing out of wealth more evenly across society, a spreading around of resources.

clue.text: National upheaval as a recipe for creating emigre?

parts.note: read the solution as an instruction: change the letters of the word regime and you get emigre

explanation.surface: A political revolution is mocked as a way of manufacturing exiles.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the second word of the solution acts as an anagram signal on the first, which rearranges into EMIGRE. The question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A forced replacement of a country's government is a political overturning on a national scale.

clue.text: Horror brought by low grade — extra study required

parts.note: D is a poor mark in exam grading
to read a subject is to study it, as at university

explanation.surface: A student is appalled to get a poor mark and be told to do more work.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is a strong fear, a near synonym of horror as a noun.

clue.text: Stop one half of an internal passage?

parts.note: semi- is the prefix meaning half
the colon is part of the large intestine, a passage inside the body

explanation.surface: A question about halting halfway along some passage indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: In punctuation a stop is any mark that pauses a sentence, and this one is such a mark.

clue.text: One may find a way through this book

definitions.text: One may find a way through this book

parts.words: One may find a way through this book
parts.note: the surface suggests a guide to a difficult text, but literally it is a booklet showing routes for drivers

explanation.definitionFit: A motoring atlas lets a traveller find a route, a way, across country.

clue.text: Harmful creature given a shout of disapproval — object of fear

parts.note: a bug is an insect, often a harmful pest
boo is what a crowd shouts at something it dislikes

explanation.surface: A nasty insect gets jeered and becomes something people dread.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugaboo is a bugbear, an imagined source of dread or anxiety.

clue.text: TV critic who shocked many — and not all fusty nannies

indicators.note: not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A broadcaster outraged viewers, though some stuffy nursemaids were unbothered.
explanation.walkthrough: Kenneth Tynan, the critic, was the first to say a famous four-letter swear word on British television, in 1965.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenneth Tynan was the theatre critic whose expletive on a BBC programme caused a national scandal.

clue.text: Getting better? No, the opposite, when it comes to those people facing death

indicators.note: the opposite says the order of the reading is turned round, so facing comes first instead of after

parts.note: on can mean facing or set against, as in a house on the sea
them is the pronoun for those people
end is a euphemism for death

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the dying are recovering, and is told they are doing the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'those people facing death' as them on (facing) end; 'the opposite' swaps that order, so 'facing' leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone recovering from illness is improving, healing back towards full health.

clue.text: Alluring, full of Eastern sparkle

indicators.note: full of means holding something inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: glam is short for glamorous, alluring

explanation.surface: Something glamorous has an oriental shimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a flash or glint of light, a sparkle as a noun.

clue.text: Salt mixed in a gelatin

indicators.note: mixed tells us the letters are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook adds salt and stirs it into some gelatin.
explanation.walkthrough: Alginates are salts of alginic acid and are used, like gelatin, as thickeners in food.
explanation.definitionFit: An alginate is a chemical salt derived from seaweed acid, used as a gelling agent.

clue.text: Instant deals negotiated somewhere in New York

indicators.note: negotiated suggests the letters are worked over and rearranged as in a bargain

explanation.surface: Quick bargains are struck in a Manhattan business setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Staten Island is one of the five boroughs making up New York City.

clue.text: Doctor's pronouncement — take time off for a bit

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: take off tells us to remove a letter from the word for pronouncement
take off tells us to remove a letter from the word for pronouncement

parts.note: a dictum is an authoritative pronouncement

explanation.surface: A doctor declares that the patient should rest from work for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take time off' is split around 'time': the time letter comes out of the word for a pronouncement, and 'Doctor's' gives the medical officer in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small quantity, a little amount of something.

clue.text: Gordon? Crooked, but keeping clear of all charges

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: bent means crooked, dishonest
a net sum is what remains after all deductions

explanation.surface: A dishonest man called Gordon somehow avoids all the accusations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gordon Bennett!' is a British exclamation of surprise, so the setter asks what follows Gordon; 'charges' misleads towards crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The two words make a familiar exclamatory phrase, so the surname is what completes the first name given.

clue.text: Does prohibition-buster have the ability to provide a conduit for trade?

parts.note: can means to be able
Al Capone made his fortune smuggling alcohol during US Prohibition

explanation.surface: Is a bootlegger capable of setting up a route for goods?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'Can Al?', Al being Capone.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is an artificial waterway built to carry goods by barge.

clue.text: Deputy union man faces endless distress

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers
Bert is a man's name

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is dropped from the word for distress

parts.note: woe is distress or sorrow

explanation.surface: The trade union's deputy leader is met with unending misery.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-in-command is the next person in rank after the leader, a deputy.

clue.text: Adherent's mainstay — one set of holy books

parts.note: a prop is a support, a mainstay
taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A believer's main support is a collection of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A proponent supports or advocates a cause, as an adherent does.

clue.text: Hormone can make one get so randy, initially

indicators.note: can make says the letters can be reworked to form the answer
initially picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A hormone is blamed for making a person feel very amorous.
explanation.definitionFit: Oestrogen is the primary female sex hormone.

clue.text: Old fossils, who caused trouble to the Israelites?

definitions.meaning: extinct shelled creatures whose coiled remains are common fossils

definitions.text: who caused trouble to the Israelites?
definitions.meaning: an ancient people east of the Jordan who fought Israel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A question about which old relics plagued the people of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both fossil cephalopods and the Biblical tribe descended from Ammon.

clue.text: Dish bringing torment to little fellow

indicators.note: to means added onto, so the torment word follows the fellow

parts.note: Tiny Tim, the small boy in Dickens, makes Tim a little fellow
bale is an old word for torment or woe

explanation.surface: A meal causes misery for a small boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbale is a dish cooked in a drum-shaped mould.

clue.text: Fool in part of trench nearest enemy

definitions.meaning: the forward end of a sap, a siege trench dug towards the enemy

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a dimwit and the head of a military sap trench.

clue.text: America backing old tribe in Africa

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: Dan was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: The United States supports an ancient tribe in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is a country in north-east Africa, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Gross charlatan taking in Europe's foremost financier

indicators.note: taking in means letting something inside, so one piece sits within the others

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for gross, twelve dozen
a sham is a fraud or impostor

indicators.note: foremost picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A coarse fraudster cons Europe's leading money man.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas Gresham was a Tudor financier who founded the Royal Exchange in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gresham was a sixteenth-century English merchant and royal financial agent.

clue.text: Most religious? Not one English composer

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letters named are left out of the word

parts.note: holiest means most religious
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Asking about piety, the clue names a composer who is not English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English' looks like part of the definition, English composer, but it gives E to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets.

clue.text: Run away from salons seen to be terrible

indicators.note: away from says the letter leaves the word for salons

parts.note: parlours are reception rooms, salons
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone flees drawing rooms that look awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlous means dangerously bad or perilous, a dire state.

clue.text: Go, start off, with green clearly observable

indicators.note: start off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone starts off with a green light that everyone can see.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and not hidden, plainly visible to all.

clue.text: Looking like a star with stuff in show? The opposite

indicators.note: in says one word goes inside the other
the opposite says the order stated is reversed, so show goes inside stuff rather than the reverse

parts.note: to stuff is to fill full, to sate
to tell can mean to show or reveal

explanation.surface: A performer stuffed into a show looks like a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken straight, 'in' would put stuff inside show; 'The opposite' turns that round, so show sits inside stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellate is a botanical word for star-shaped, radiating from a centre.

clue.text: One desiring solitude — magnificent but ultimately twisted

indicators.note: ultimately twisted says the final pair of letters is turned round

parts.note: great means magnificent

explanation.surface: Something splendid ends up warped.
explanation.walkthrough: Greta Garbo is famous for the line 'I want to be alone'; GREAT has its last two letters swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo, the film star, was renowned for wanting to be left alone.

clue.text: Undo the side nut somehow to get at the side

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some new way

explanation.surface: A mechanic loosens a nut on the side panel to reach inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' appears twice: the first is fodder, the second, with 'the', is the definition, a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: Southend United is an English football club, and a side is a team.
